title: Sensex, Nifty Fall for Third Session as Crude Tops $110 on Saudi Attacks
excerpt: The Sensex opened 0.5% lower at 73,343.3 and the Nifty fell 0.54% to 22,687.75 on Thursday, October 22, as Brent above $110 stoked inflation fears and every NSE sector traded in the red.
body:
• The Sensex fell 0.5% to 73,343.3 and the Nifty 50 declined 0.54% to 22,687.75 at the 9:15 a.m. open on Thursday, October 22, a third straight losing session, according to Livemint.
  • Brent crude rose 1.6% to $110.6 a barrel after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia prompted the United States to order some diplomats and their families to leave its missions in the kingdom.
  • The fall was broad: by 9:21 a.m. the Sensex was down 494 points at 73,215 and the Nifty down 222 points at 22,589, with the Nifty Metal index down over 2% and mid- and small-cap indices down about 1.6%.
  • For investors, the levels to watch are Sensex support at 73,200-73,500 and resistance at 74,300-74,500, while minutes of the RBI's last meeting show some rate-setters see further hikes as possible if oil-driven inflation persists.

Indian equities opened lower for a third consecutive session on Thursday as crude oil above $110 a barrel revived inflation worries and weak Asian markets offered no support. The Sensex fell 0.5% to 73,343.3 at the open and the Nifty 50 declined 0.54% to 22,687.75, Livemint reported, extending a week in which the two benchmarks have shed 1.4% and 1.5% respectively, according to Reuters.

Selling deepened in the first minutes of trade. The Sensex fell as much as 705 points and the Nifty touched an intraday low of 22,564, dragged down by HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, Mahindra & Mahindra, Maruti Suzuki, Bharti Airtel, Power Grid and Bajaj Finance, Upstox reported. As of 9:21 a.m., the Sensex was down 494 points at 73,215 and the Nifty was down 222 points at 22,589. Market breadth was heavily negative, with 2,361 shares falling against 691 advancing on the NSE.

Oil Is the Problem

Brent crude futures rose 1.3% to $110.3 a barrel in the Reuters pre-market report and 1.6% to $110.6 in Livemint's account of the open, after more attacks in Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis prompted the United States to order some diplomats and family members to leave its missions in the kingdom. Brent has surged more than 80% this year amid disruptions to Persian Gulf oil flows caused by the US-Iran war, Livemint noted.

For India the transmission is direct. The country imports the bulk of its energy requirements, so sustained triple-digit crude can increase inflation, strain the fiscal deficit and hit corporate profits, Reuters reported. That concern is now inside the central bank as well: members of the Reserve Bank of India's rate-setting panel indicated that further rate hikes may be needed to curb inflation, though they stopped short of endorsing an aggressive tightening cycle given the risks to growth, according to minutes of the committee's meeting released on Wednesday.

"Strong external headwinds in the form of elevated crude prices and high US bond yields are emboldening bears to build short positions in the market."

— V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments

Broader Market Takes the Harder Hit

Every major NSE sector gauge traded lower, led by the Nifty Metal index's fall of over 2%, with Bank, Financial Services, Auto, FMCG, Media, Pharma, Realty, Healthcare, Consumer Durables and Oil & Gas indices down between 0.8% and 1.5%, Upstox reported. Coal India was the top Nifty loser, down 2.5% to Rs 397, while Power Grid, Dr Reddy's Labs, Nestle India, Hindalco and Tata Steel fell between 1.5% and 2.3%. Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services fell as much as 6.5% to Rs 278 despite reporting a 55% rise in second-quarter net profit. Eternal, Bharti Airtel, Infosys and HCL Technologies were among the few gainers.

Asia set the tone. Japan's Nikkei fell 0.96%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng declined 2.73%, China's Shanghai Composite dropped 1.4% and South Korea's Kospi fell 2.27%, as mixed earnings from major US technology companies renewed questions about the sustainability of AI-related investment, according to Upstox and Livemint.

What to Watch

Thursday is Sensex weekly expiry, which can amplify swings as traders close or roll derivatives positions. Kotak Neo's Shrikant Chouhan pointed to 73,700 and 73,500 as key support zones, with a move towards 74,000-74,500 possible if the index holds above them, while Choice Equity Broking's Sachin Gupta put immediate support at 73,200-73,500 and resistance at 74,300-74,500, with a put-call ratio of 0.95 signalling a balanced but cautious setup.

Two offsets are worth noting for diaspora investors watching Indian portfolios from abroad. Foreign investors bought Indian shares worth Rs 10.22 billion ($108.19 million) on Wednesday, a second session of buying in three, according to provisional data cited by Reuters. The Jio Platforms IPO also drew focus: the $3.2 billion issue was fully subscribed within hours of launch on Wednesday, Reuters reported. Neither offset changes the near-term driver — while Brent holds above $110, Indian equities are trading an oil story first.
